subject: Emotions
title: Why We Say 'Yuck'
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Why We Say 'Yuck'.

hook.text: The word 'disgust' comes from the French 'desgoust'—literally meaning bad taste.

buildup.text: Every culture has a disgust word tied to oral rejection. In Japanese, it's 'kimochi warui'—bad feeling.

discovery.text: Paul Rozin found that disgust is contagious. A clean glass touched to a cockroach becomes 'dirty' forever.

twist.text: Even imaginary contact triggers disgust. A sterilized cockroach in juice still makes people refuse to drink.

climax.text: Disgust follows magical thinking, not logic. Knowing something is safe doesn't stop the feeling.

punchline.text: Your gut overrules your brain every single time.

quiz.question: What does the French root 'desgoust' mean?
